checks.evidence: Focused 2026-10-21 observation: one yellow sun and three differently sized cyan, blue and purple spheres were visible across startup and seek states. With real UI seeking at 0,3,6,9,12,24,36,48,17 and 73 seconds, a native 800-pixel wheel zoom-out and 70-pixel vertical camera drag improved the view; all samples used the same 1440x900 viewport and unchanged camera after that adjustment. The 0 and 48 rendered configurations visually repeated and individual objects moved between samples, but the giant purple sphere still completely hid Mercury/Terra at several samples (notably 6 seconds), clipped at the top/bottom at others, and obscured their geometric centers. Consequently complete circular trajectories, individual 12/24/48-second rendered periods and all fixed geometric phases, including reload stability, could not be established within the preregistered 2-degree-plus-rounding/2-CSS-pixel tolerances. Source phase candidates 0,1,2 radians and angle readouts were not substituted for missing rendered geometry evidence. S1 remains unverified rather than inferred pass or geometry failure.

Action: Opened the scene and repeatedly reloaded in the same origin. Expected: Initial time zero, 1x, running, null selection and overview, followed by motion. Observed: Load-barrier snapshots showed 0.01–0.05 seconds, 1x, Playing, overview, disabled tracking and explicit No planet selected; subsequent time and rendered positions advanced. Elapsed load time was not treated as a reset defect.

Action: Paused during motion, sought 73, waited 3.1069 seconds, selected planets and orbited/zoomed while paused, then resumed at the selected speed. Expected: Frozen time/positions, usable selection/camera and continuous resume. Observed: 73.00 seconds and Mercury 30.0 degrees remained exact; the unchanged-camera 462000-pixel scene crop had zero different decoded pixels. Camera and selection responded while paused. Resume continued from the sought state, and timed 0.25x/2x/4x samples followed their expected rates without a reset.

Action: Set 0.25x, 2x and 4x while paused at 17, waited at least 3.1 seconds each, resumed and measured paired page-clock endpoints in the sole visible review scene; also changed among these speeds while playing. Expected: No seek or position reset, rates proportional to speed and preserved relative orbits. Observed: Paused time remained 17.00 in all cases. 0.25x advanced 17.06→17.86 in 3.2027 seconds; 2x advanced 17.45→23.85 in 3.2044 seconds; 4x advanced 17.91→30.71 in 3.2031 seconds, within preregistered tolerance. Playing 1.5x→2x preserved Terra/tracking/playback, with 17.57→17.60 over 0.011 seconds. Independent individual-planet angular samples retained the 30/15/7.5 degrees per simulation-second relationship; rendered motion continued without a speed-change position reset.

Action: Used the real time range at 0, 17, 30, 73 and 120; revisited 30/17/73 after playback, speed and selection changes, then repeated after reload. Expected: Immediate paused state, fixed phases and identical rendered state at identical time/camera/selection. Observed: Angle triples were 0/57.3/114.6; 150/312.3/242.1; 180/147.3/339.6; 30/72.3/302.1; and 0/57.3/294.6 degrees respectively. All seeks paused and changed the rendered positions. Repeat 30/17/73 and their after-reload counterparts each had zero differing pixels in a 462000-pixel decoded scene crop with Mercury selected and the same standard overview; canvas bounds were x10/y10, 940x620 CSS pixels. Fractional 17.25 through valid restore showed 157.5/316.0/244.0 degrees. Occlusion limits full trajectory measurement under S1, not the observed repeated rendered state.

Action: Sought 119, set 4x, resumed across the endpoint, waited 3.2032 seconds, then sought 73 and resumed. Expected: Stop exactly at 120 without wrapping and allow earlier playback. Observed: 119.91 Playing became 120.00 Paused and remained at the endpoint during the wait; earlier seek resumed to 73.90 Playing at 4x.

Action: Correlated index.html with the loaded CDN resource and inspected rendered orbit/zoom responses. Expected: Genuine Three.js three-dimensional geometry, depth and camera perspective changes. Observed: HTTP resource timing recorded the Three.js 0.124.0 CDN script. The source constructs WebGLRenderer, PerspectiveCamera and SphereGeometry meshes. Native camera drags changed which shaded spheres occluded one another and their perspective arrangement; wheel input changed apparent size in both camera modes. The scene is rendered 3D, although its intersecting oversized geometry is visually problematic.

Expected: Capture preserves live state; immutable, uniquely identified entries display all fields and time-derived angles. Observed: A ID obs-1792502587868-0 displayed 30s, 2x, terra, tracking and 180.0/147.3/339.6 degrees and stayed byte-for-byte unchanged after live time/speed/selection/mode/playback edits. Playing capture displayed its precise captured time 0.09460000004768372, 1x and null overview with 2.8/58.7/115.3 degrees; its ID and values survived reload without altering the live defaults. Import/export retained IDs and order. Imported 17.25 produced 157.5/316.0/244.0 degrees despite supplied angles 999, and remained the same after reload.

Action: Selected Mercury, Terra and Neptune individually through canvas native clicks and all three list buttons while paused at 0 and again while playing at 0.25x. Expected: Shared selection, visible highlight and information in both routes. Observed: Canvas positions (640,380), (350,450), (100,150) selected Mercury/Terra/Neptune respectively in both states; the list routes selected the same objects. Each switched the highlighted sphere/list button and information. Playing list samples were Mercury at 0.15, Terra at 0.22 and Neptune at 0.29 seconds; paused samples stayed 0.00.

Action: Compared selected names/periods/angles across canvas/list selection, playback, five seeks and null-selection restores. Expected: Matching selected information, updated angular state and explicit cleared no-selection state. Observed: Mercury/Terra/Neptune information showed 12/24/48-second periods and the phase-consistent angle triples recorded in S5; the observed highlighted objects moved with those updates. Startup and null overview restores showed No planet selected and removed all selection highlighting. Fractional Mercury tracking restore showed 157.5 degrees at 17.25. Dense occlusion is disclosed under S1/V1 rather than claiming fully measured circular trajectories.

Action: Tracked Mercury while playing, paused and seeking; switched to Terra and Neptune; tried tracking after a null-selection restore. Expected: Centered target, immediate seeks, synchronized selection/info/target with preserved live state and rejection without a selection. Observed: Mercury tracking samples at approximately 17.32, 17.74 and 18.17 seconds over a 3.4854-second visible interval kept its visible center within roughly 51 CSS pixels of the 940x620 canvas center, below the 62-pixel tolerance; seeking 17 immediately recentered it. Terra tracking visibly centered its highlighted sphere, and changing list selections retained speed/playback and natural time progression. Null overview at 30/1.5x rejected tracking with Select a planet before tracking and unchanged state.

Action: Returned from tracking to overview during the ordered scenario and at paused 30/73/120 and both viewport sizes. Expected: Full-system visibility while preserving selection/time/speed/playback. Observed: State was preserved, but overview did not show the full system: around 38 seconds Neptune filled essentially the entire canvas; at 30 and 73 the large purple sphere was clipped at multiple edges and obscured the sun and other planets. Source index.html constructs planet radii as period/4 (3,6,12) at orbit radii 5,8,11, with overview distance 24; the overview handler merely changes view mode, not framing. This is an observed full-system framing failure, not a state-reset claim.

Action: Restored selected tracking A after unrelated live edits and manual orbit/zoom, and restored null overview snapshots at 30 and 0, repeating restores at the same desktop size. Expected: Atomic paused restoration with synchronized fields, cleared null selection and deterministic standard full-system overview/selected tracking framing. Observed: Time, speed readout, selection, mode, angles and paused playback restored correctly and null restoration cleared selected information. Overview restore reset camera consistently (0-time repeated crop had zero changed pixels), but the standard overview still clipped/occluded most of the system, including the sun at time 30. Thus the required standard full-system framing fails. Tracking restores visibly returned to the selected target; precise repeated-tracking image equality was not certified because one click did not activate and another comparison had a scroll alignment difference. Neither comparison is counted as a deterministic-camera defect.

Action: Performed native drags and wheel zoom in overview and tracking, each while playing and paused, including reverse wheel zoom after restore. Action: Inspected labels and feedback through playback, snapshots, restore, invalid JSON, capacity and quota cases. Expected: Understandable, consistent current-state and operation feedback. Snapshot lines are dense and include raw long fractional times. Rating 2: usable with recurring ambiguity/inconsistency, independently of mobile occlusion.

Deleting obs-1792502616470-1 retained A and obs-1792502616750-2 in order; replacement obs-1792502617336-2 appended without collision. Live 73/2x/Terra/overview/paused remained unchanged.

Action: At desktop and mobile used Enter, range Home/End/arrows, Tab/Shift+Tab and textarea selection/deletion for every primary DOM control; specifically tabbed from Capture to Restore and backward from JSON to Delete, waited 100ms and pressed Enter. Expected: Meaningful names, visible stable focus, normal keyboard activation and no trap. Observed: Static controls and textarea work and show yellow focus outlines; mobile immediate Restore/Delete sometimes activated. However snapshot buttons are rebuilt every animation frame even while paused: focus falls to BODY before a normal delayed activation. Desktop Enter then left live time 73 instead of restoring 0 and did not delete any of the three entries. Source loop→ui→draw replaces snaps.innerHTML and recreates buttons each frame. This is an observed unstable-focus/keyboard-operability failure, not merely a locator detachment.
